title: The Last Train
premise: A fictional writer observes a station, shapes a poem, then makes a small book. Combinations produce drafts and forms, not a claim that literary value has a recipe.

items.label: Chapbook
items.description:
Your station poem, stitched into a small book.

The rails hum after you
have gone. Stay a while.
The platform holds your name.
Stay a while.

items.label: Departure board
items.description: The last destination blinks away. One unlit row remains.

items.label: Departure sketch
items.description: An empty platform, with one name written below it.

items.label: Enjambed poem
items.description:
The rails hum after you
have gone. The empty platform
keeps your name.

items.label: First draft
items.description: The train is gone. I listen to the station. I remember a goodbye.

items.label: Inked form
items.description: Ink touches the raised letters, ready to leave their mirror image on paper.

items.label: Line break
items.description: Try ending the first line after “you”, before the sentence is finished.

items.label: Memory
items.description: Someone has gone. You find yourself asking them to stay.

items.label: Printed booklet
items.description:
The printer presses the poem onto sheets, then folds them into this little book.

The rails hum after you
have gone. Stay a while.
The platform holds your name.
Stay a while.

items.label: Reading aloud
items.description: Reading aloud, the editor catches the long third line. Try “The platform holds your name.”

items.label: Refrain
items.description: Let “Stay a while” return twice: once addressed to the traveller, once to the memory.

items.label: Refrain poem
items.description:
The rails hum after you
have gone. Stay a while.
The empty platform keeps your name.
Stay a while.

items.label: Revised poem
items.description:
The rails hum after you
have gone. Stay a while.
The platform holds your name.
Stay a while.

items.label: Sound notes
items.description: An observation: the rails keep humming after the train has gone.

items.label: Station poem
items.description:
The rails hum after you have gone.
The empty platform keeps your name.

items.label: Station sounds
items.description: Wheels click over a joint; after the train leaves, a low note lingers in the rails.

items.label: Type form
items.description: The revised poem is set in movable type, ready for ink.

retire.reason: The original is incorporated into this recognizable derived thing.

recipes.description: The sentence now continues beyond “you” and “platform” across line endings. The change delays what follows; it need not be better.
“Stay a while” returns, turning a request into a refrain.
The spoken test shortens the third line. This is one editorial choice, not the correct poem.
The printer inks and presses the type onto sheets before folding the printed sheets. These workshop steps are compressed into this action.

retire.reason: The original is incorporated into this recognizable derived thing.

stages.title: The last train
stages.speaker: The writer
stages.motivation: Everyone is leaving, and the station has its own music. Make a station poem from what you notice.

area.label: The last train
area.travelText: We are taking the useful things with us. Earlier creations remain where we made them.

stages.title: At the reading table
stages.speaker: The editor
stages.motivation: Try holding the sentence over a line ending, then let “Stay a while” return. Read each version; make the revised poem for our little press.

area.label: At the reading table
area.travelText: We are taking the useful things with us. Earlier creations remain where we made them.

caches.label: The editor’s marked examples
caches.narrative: Examples demonstrate a line break, a returning refrain and reading aloud. They are techniques, not mandatory steps in all poems.

stages.title: The little press
stages.speaker: The printer
stages.motivation: Let the poem leave this room. Make a stitched chapbook.

area.label: The little press
area.travelText: We are taking the useful things with us. Earlier creations remain where we made them.

caches.label: The printer’s supplies
caches.narrative: The small press has paper, folding instructions, type, ink and binding thread.
